title_card: Turn your Morse key or paddle into a Bluetooth key

beats.text: Want to practise Morse on your own paddle, without a radio, and without a cable to the laptop?
BLE-Key is a tiny Bluetooth box that sits between your key and the app.
It's built around a Seeed XIAO board: the ESP32-S3, or the nRF52840.
The paddle goes into the three and a half millimetre jack. The tip is dit, the ring is dah.
The box makes no sound itself. It just sends exact keying edges, and the LED shows when you key.
There's a version with a battery, too.
Power it over USB-C. In Longpath, it shows up as a paddle. Tap it, and you're connected.
Now the app makes the sidetone, decodes what you send, and shows your timing.
It works with straight keys, single paddles and iambic paddles, on phone, tablet or Mac.
Firmware and enclosure are open on GitHub. Print the case, solder the jack, flash the board.
Or get a parts kit or a finished key from the Ramus Labs shop.

closing: Links to the shop, to Longpath and to GitHub are in the description. Seventy-three!

endcard.platforms: Works with Longpath on iPhone · iPad · Mac · Android
